admission.justification: Key omission and variable-value scrubbing with ordinary-value preservation are proved by the named passing redaction cases; single-file member of the family.

applicability: Every argument value written to a log line or detail file.
conditions: Credential-naming keys are dropped at any depth.
Credential-variable values of six or more chars are scrubbed wherever they occur; shorter texts and ordinary values (home paths included) stay whole.
exclusions: Values under six characters, which are never searched.
The call outcome itself, which redaction never changes.

evidence: mcp/tests/test_tool_answer_table.py redaction tests including test_short_credential_variable_value_is_omitted, test_ordinary_env_value_is_written and test_home_folder_path_stays_whole (passing in the R6 run); documentary corpus notes/reports/l108-f14-documentary-successor/worker-documentary-evidence.json (SHA 6601bb084849a73554f0e385cf90028966b8bbe07831333cc81529e7b6e89725); A8 documentary corpus notes/reports/l108-f14-documentary-successor-a8/worker-documentary-evidence.json

statement: No credential in a log (amended rule 3): credential-naming keys are dropped; the value of a variable whose name names a credential (key, token, secret, password, passwd, credential, auth, cookie, any case) is left out wherever it occurs in an argument, from six characters on; every other environment value is ordinary text and is written.
